item.research_question: How can noble-metal-free heterogeneous catalysts be developed to realize the aerobic oxidation of C–H bonds at low temperatures with high selectivity?
item.material_system: Mesoporous Mn0.5Ce0.5Ox solid solution (Mn/Ce atomic ratio 1:1)
item.processing_route: Slow hydrolysis of Mn(II) acetate and Ce(IV) methoxyethoxide precursors in the presence of ionic liquid BmimTf2N template at 50 °C for 24 h, followed by solidification at 200 °C for 2 h, extraction of the ionic liquid via ethanol reflux, and thermal treatment at 500 °C for 2 h in air.
item.test_conditions: Cyclohexane oxidation: 100 °C, 1 MPa O2, 12 h reaction time; CO oxidation: 1% CO in dry air, atmospheric pressure, flow rate 10 ml min−1; Other hydrocarbons: 110–120 °C, 1 MPa O2.
key_findings: Cyclohexane conversion reached 17.7% with 81% selectivity for KA oil (cyclohexanone/cyclohexanol) at 100 °C.
The catalyst achieved 100% CO conversion at approximately 90 °C, with a T50 of 60 °C.
XPS analysis revealed that Mn4+ species dominate the surface with 87% content.
The atomic ratio of 'reactive' oxygen species (Oβ) on the surface reached 44.1%.
The catalyst maintained activity for at least 20 runs in cyclohexane oxidation without significant loss.
The average crystalline size of the Mn0.5Ce0.5Ox@500 sample was calculated to be 1.4 nm.
The H2 consumption of the Mn0.5Ce0.5Ox@500 sample reached 4.22 mmol g−1.
Oxidation of cyclohexane could proceed at a temperature as low as 80 °C.
item.mechanism: The high activity is attributed to the formation of a Mn0.5Ce0.5Ox solid solution with an ultrahigh manganese doping concentration in the CeO2 cubic fluorite lattice, which leads to maximum active surface oxygens for C–H bond activation and highly reducible Mn4+ ions that facilitate the rapid migration of oxygen vacancies from the bulk to the surface.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the self-assembly strategy with ionic liquids will inspire more designs of mesoporous oxide solid solutions for specific tasks in the near future.
quotes: Here we report the synthesis of a mesoporous Mn0.5Ce0.5Ox solid solution that is highly active for the selective oxidation of hydrocarbons under mild conditions (100–120 °C).
The high activity can be attributed to the formation of a Mn0.5Ce0.5Ox solid solution with an ultrahigh manganese doping concentration in the CeO2 cubic fluorite lattice.
The Mn0.5Ce0.5Ox@500 catalyst enables the 100% CO conversion at around 90 °C.
